newsitem.title: USA: Consumer group warns Wall St on Shell-Texaco merger.
newsitem.headline: Consumer group warns Wall St on Shell-Texaco merger.

text.p: A consumer group warned Wall Street analysts not to assume the proposed merger of Shell Oil and Texaco Inc's western U.S. refining and marketing operations was a done deal, according to a memorandum released Sunday.

Citizen Action said the market power that the merged company would have on the West Coast could spark the same antitrust concerns the Federal Trade Commission raised when it recently rejected the merger of two office supply companies.

"Based on our analysis of the FTC's opposition to the Staples/Office Depot merger, we believe that there is a high probability that the FTC will seek either to require the divestiture of significant West Coast refining and marketing assets, or to block the Shell/Texaco merger itself," Edwin Rothschild, Citizen Action's energy program director, wrote in a June 26 memo to oil industry investment analysts.

"While there are many differences between the Staples/Office Depot merger and the Shell/Texaco merger, there are a number of essential similarities that should give investors serious cause for concern if they believe or assume FTC approval is a foregone conclusion or simple formality," he said.
Rothschild's comments in the memo matched a letter that he sent to the FTC urging the agency to block the oil companies' plan.

He highlighted that Shell and Texaco statements had failed to point out that after their merger, they would have 23 percent of West Coast refining capacity, and 17 percent of the California retail gasoline market, much larger shares than the merged operation would have nationwide.
